EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  

1. Identification Strategy  

Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with staggered treatment adoption, estimated in an “event-study‐style” two-way-fixed-effects panel.  

Rationale  
• The IRRC snapshots give discrete dates (1990, ’93, ’95, ’98, ’00, ’02, ’04) at which we observe whether a firm has added or removed antitakeover provisions. Those changes create naturally staggered treatment timing.  
• Many firms change their G-index/E-index during the sample (e.g., adopt poison pill in 1998). Comparing the announcement-period abnormal return (CAR) of acquisitions the same firm undertakes before vs. after the governance change—and differencing out common shocks with time FEs—yields a within-firm causal estimate.  
• A DID avoids relying solely on cross-sectional comparisons (which are confounded by permanent firm traits) and does not require an external instrument.  
• The outcome (CAR[-1,+1]) is observed at the acquisition-announcement day, so the “event” (acquisition) is nested inside the broader governance-change window, satisfying the timing requirement of DID.  

Equation  

CAR_{i,d} = β · PostATP_{i,d} + γ′X_{i,d} + δ_i + τ_t + ε_{i,d}  

where PostATP_{i,d}=1 if deal d by firm i is announced after the first IRRC snapshot in which i’s G-index rises by ≥2 points (or crosses the high-G threshold), 0 if before; δ_i = firm FE; τ_t = calendar-year FE (or snapshot-year×industry FE). β is the causal effect of weaker governance on acquirer returns. We also estimate a dynamic event-study:

CAR_{i,d}=∑_{k=-4}^{+4} β_k · 1{event time = k}+ …  

2. Treatment and Control  

• Treatment variable: Increase in entrenchment. Main specification: a binary PostATP that equals 1 if, at the IRRC snapshot immediately preceding the acquisition, the firm’s G-index ≥10 (top tercile) or its E-index ≥3; 0 otherwise. Alternative: continuous ∆G or ∆E.  
• Treated observations: Acquisitions announced after the firm first becomes high-entrenchment.  
• Control observations: (i) Acquisitions by the same firm before the governance change (within-firm control) and (ii) acquisitions by firms that never become high-entrenchment during the sample (between-firm control that pins down calendar shocks).  
• Treatment timing: The IRRC publication year in which the firm moves into the high-G/E category. Acquisition announcement date (t=0 for CAR window) must fall strictly after that snapshot to be coded as “post.”  
• No running variable/cutoff is used (not RDD).  

3. Key Identifying Assumptions  

A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of changing ATPs, acquirer CARs at announcement would have evolved similarly for treated and control observations.  
Plausibility: Firms only rarely plan ATP adoptions around specific future acquisitions, and we difference out firm FE and rich time×industry FE. We will probe using pre-trend coefficients in the event-study.  

A2. No simultaneous shocks that coincide with ATP adoption and directly affect CARs.  
Plausibility: IRRC snapshots are calendar based and not tied to M&A waves; nevertheless, firms may cluster ATP changes around other strategic shifts. We control for contemporaneous changes in leverage, cash, Q, etc.  

A3. Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA): One firm’s adoption of ATPs does not affect another firm’s acquisition return.  
Plausibility: Reasonable in diversified U.S. market.  

4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation  

T1. Endogenous adoption of ATPs in anticipation of a specific forthcoming acquisition.  
Mitigation:  
• Drop acquisitions announced within six months after a governance change (“ashen” window).  
• Event-study pre-trend test; if β_{-1},β_{-2},… not significant, anticipation is limited.  

T2. Sample selection—only acquisitions that are completed enter SDC; bad deals may be withdrawn. If governance quality affects withdrawal probability, estimates on completed deals are biased.  
Mitigation:  
• Replicate analysis using the broader set of announced deals (completed + withdrawn) where CARs are still observable.  
• Heckman selection model as robustness.  

T3. Mis-measurement of treatment timing because IRRC snapshots are every 2–3 years.  
Mitigation:  
• Assign adoption year as fiscal year midpoint between snapshots and perform sensitivity tests using alternative timing assumptions (forward/backward one year).  
• Use E-index (fewer provisions) which changes less frequently, reducing timing error.  

5. R Code Outline  

```r
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# PACKAGES
library(data.table)   # fast data wrangling
library(fixest)       # TWFE regressions
library(bacondecomp)  # staggered-DID decomposition
library(ggplot2)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. LOAD DATA
sdc   <- fread("sdc_acquisitions.csv")       # deal-level
crsp  <- fread("crsp_daily.csv")             # returns
gov   <- fread("irrc_governance.csv")        # G- & E-index by snapshot
comp  <- fread("compustat.csv")              # firm fundamentals

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. VARIABLE CONSTRUCTION
## event-study CAR[-1,+1]
# assume a pre-computed file with car column per deal
car   <- fread("car_window.csv")             # deal_id, CAR

## merge all
dt <- merge(sdc, car, by = "deal_id")
dt <- merge(dt, comp, by = c("permno","fyear"), all.x = TRUE)

# merge governance: find most recent snapshot before ann_date
setkey(gov, permno, snapshot_date)
setkey(dt,  permno, ann_date)

dt <- gov[dt, roll = -Inf]          # last observation carried forward

## High entrenchment dummy
dt[, highG := as.integer(G_index >= 10)]     # top tercile
dt[, highE := as.integer(E_index >= 3)]

## Identify first entry into highG
dt[, first_highG_year := min(ann_year[highG==1]), by = permno]
dt[, treated := as.integer(ann_year >= first_highG_year & !is.na(first_highG_year))]

## Post variable
dt[, post := treated]

## Clean sample
dt <- dt[!is.na(CAR) & ann_year>=1990 & ann_year<=2003]

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 3. MAIN SPECIFICATION: TWFE DID
spec1 <- feols(CAR ~ post + payment_method + rel_deal_size + cash_holdings +
                     leverage + TobinsQ | permno + ann_year,
               data = dt, cluster = ~permno)
summary(spec1)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 4. EVENT-STUDY
## event time k = year_ann - first_highG_year
dt[, event_time := ann_year - first_highG_year]
dt <- dt[event_time >= -4 & event_time <= 4]  # window
est_evt <- feols(CAR ~ i(event_time, ref = -1) +
                       payment_method + rel_deal_size |
                       permno + ann_year,
                 data = dt, cluster = ~permno)
iplot(est_evt)  # visually inspect pre-trends

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 5. ROBUSTNESS: Bacon decomposition for negative weighting
bacon_results <- bacon(CAR ~ post, data = dt, id_var = "permno",
                       time_var = "ann_year")
plot(bacon_results)

# Alternative robustness: continuous ΔG
dt[, dG := G_index - shift(G_index), by = permno]
spec_cont <- feols(CAR ~ dG + controls | permno + ann_year,
                   data = dt[!is.na(dG)], cluster = ~permno)
```

6. Expected Results  

Theory (agency view) predicts β < 0. Entrenched managers overpay and pursue value-destroying deals, so the CAR of acquisitions announced after governance weakens should be lower by roughly 1–1.5 percentage points (CAR window [-1,+1]) compared to deals by otherwise similar firms.  

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)  

C1: Parallel pre-trend confirmed (via event-study)……… 0.8  
C2: No anticipation of treatment…………………………… 0.6  
C3: Stable composition / no selection into sample……… 0.7  
C4: Correct treatment timing………………………………… 0.6  
C5: No spillovers / SUTVA…………………………………… 0.9  

(A score of 1 indicates “clearly satisfied”; 0.8 ≈ “largely satisfied”; etc.)
